utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-16-T, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, Dragan Papic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Witness. We are going to resume our examination from yesterday. I have a few more questions, but I don't think they will take long.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: We stopped yesterday on the road linking Kaonik and Ahmici. You were approaching the roadblock. You told us that you were warned of the existence of this roadblock by Croatian civilians that you met on the road; am I not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, everything is correct. They warned me. I didn't heed their warnings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: At that point in time, as you were going along the road towards Ahmici, did you see HVO military forces?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not see any HVO forces. I only saw civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I have asked you this question because in the summary of your testimony communicated to us by the Defence, it says that you said that you were warned of the existence of this roadblock by HVO military members.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, the HVO was not there. There may have been one or two members in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Passing by the Bungalow, you didn't see anyone?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Before the Bungalow, I saw some people calling me from the bushes, actually, telling me to stop and not to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: At what time did you reach the roadblock near Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know the exact time, but it could have been between 7.00 and 7.30 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us with some precision how that roadblock had been made, what objects did it consist of, and how it was removed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: The roadblock or barricade was made out of village fences that we called Baskija, and how it was removed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you were held there for about one hour near the roadblock and that afterwards you were allowed to leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Could I have the registrar's attention, please, the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you were held there for a certain amount of time at the roadblock and that afterwards you were allowed to leave. Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Again, I continued along the main Kaonik-Vitez road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: After that evening, after having passed the roadblock, did you have any contact with a member of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not because my father was very ill, so I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: In your opinion, Witness, I refer to your military experiences, you are a professional soldier, what was the logic of this roadblock? What was the motivation, the reason, for building it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the logic nor ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, during March, April, and later -- I'm talking of March and April 1993, of course. Did you meet the accused Dragan Papic, whom you referred to yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I would see him in Vitez, in Fistas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific as to the period during which you encountered the accused Dragan Papic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm talking of the month of March and April. I can't be more specific because I really do not remember myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. Do you have any memory of meeting Dragan Papic in March or April or later in 1993?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: May I put it this way, in March and April --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness wants the names of the months to be interpreted in a dialect he understands better. Third and fourth month.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question: Do you recollect having encountered the accused Dragan Papic in the months of March or April 1993 or the months that followed, the third, fourth, and following months of that year?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not meet him. For one reason, at the time, I don't know how to put it, we were preparing to defend our village. We were digging trenches and dugouts and other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So all that you told us about the accused Dragan Papic, especially regarding his physical appearance, has to do with the previous period. You cannot give us any precise information regarding the months of March and April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I can't because we are not neighbours nor are we close friends. The distance between my house and his is three and a half to four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you know the other accused in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you have anything you would wish to say about them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could say that they are very nice people, at least that was my impression, I don't know what other people think, and I can guarantee that they did not commit the crime, from my point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: How did you meet them? What were the circumstances in which you met them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know Dragan Papic because we would meet in the Cafe Fistas. The other gentlemen I know from sight. I mean, I would see them in the street. Some of them are businessmen who had their own businesses, wholesale stores, so I would see them in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Therefore, you do not have any friendly relations with them, not even a personal acquaintanceship, just a physical contact, a visual contact?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Passing by, we would see one another. We had no friendly contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: A last question, Witness: As a member of the HVO, did you take an oath?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: In which army?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not -- no, not -- no because that is no longer the fashion, one might say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Terrier. Madam Pinter?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Males.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Let us clarify a few points. In answer to a question from the Prosecutor, you said that on the 15th of August, 1993 -- sorry, 1995, you became a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said on the 21st of August, 1995 I became a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Of which army did you become a professional soldier?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of the 3rd Guards Brigade, which is now a part of the Federation. This was a professional unit, and it is still a professional unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So you mean you signed a contract and that you are employed in the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have a three-year contract with them. When the contract expires, it may be extended if my medical reports allow it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In March or April 1993, did you sign any kind of a contract with the army?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not sign any contract.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Does that mean then that in March and April you were not a professional soldier?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: No, it was just to defend the homeland.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. In answer to a question by the Prosecutor yesterday, you said that you became an active-duty soldier at the beginning of the conflict in March 1993.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What do you consider to be the beginning of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: The war itself that broke out in our area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 16th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you mean March or April?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Then can we take it that when you told the Prosecutor it was March that you made a mistake?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was a mistake on my part.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Up until the 16th of April, 1993, were you an active-duty soldier or were you a reservist?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was in the reserves.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So there were reserves?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but not in the sense other people understand it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Crveno Brdce is or the red hillock?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a hamlet close to Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can we ask the usher to remove the first aerial photograph and to leave the aerial photograph of the Lasva River Valley that's on the board.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please turn around so that Their Honours and the Prosecution can see you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is Rijeka, all of this, and Crveno Brdce is right here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. How far is Crveno Brdce from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Crveno Brdce is about one to one and a half kilometres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How far is it from Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is really part of Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: How far was Crveno Brdce from the front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: You mean of the BH army or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the defence line in relation to the BH army.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just below the wood, you can see the wood here. They were below the wood, and we were above the woods, and in this area too. This was closer to us, to our homes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were you on Crveno Brdce to watch over your home and property or did you have any other assignments or tasks up there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: All I did was defend my property.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were on the front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were you alone up there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no. During the war, of course, I couldn't have been alone.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were there other people with you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the front line?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, all the Croats here (indicating), along here (indicating). You see, it's about 30 metres between the front line and our houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: As you said in answer to a question from the Prosecution, Mr. Grabovac, who was your superior, was he with you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, Grabovac never appeared on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You may take your seat now we won't be referring to the map any more. Do you know that persons who were not active members of the HVO were entitled to shares?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that for one reason, my wife received the shares.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And she was not an active member?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, she was not. She was not mobilised. May I just expand on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: No, there's no need. Can we take it then that the right to shares was not limited only to active duty soldiers of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was not limited to active members. Shares were given to the elderly as well and to women.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. In answer to a question from the Prosecution when discussing your movement from Podjele, according to the transcript it seems as if when you left Podjele you already knew that there was a roadblock at Ahmici. My question is: When you left Podjele did you know that there was a roadblock at Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When did you learn about it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I learnt about it at Nadoici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the importance of the Busovaca to Vitez road?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is the main communication route. I don't know what you really mean, but it is the main road leading to Zenica and Sarajevo, so it links those areas with Zenica and Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Is it of strategic importance?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: But if you just said that that is the route leading to the other towns, is it important?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is important. I said that it linked towns, Zenica, Sarajevo, and just at the crossroads near Kaonik it links onto the Sarajevo to Zenica main road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: One further question. When you saw Dragan Papic in the period when you came across him he wore a beard, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MALES (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We have no questions. Mr. Males, thank you for coming to The Hague to testify in court. You may now be released. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Puliselic, is the next witness going to enjoy any protective measures? Are you requesting measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: No. No, Mr. President, no protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Puliselic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Milicevic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Would you please introduce yourself to the court and tell us your name, your surname, your place and date of birth and your address?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: My name is Ljubica Milicevic. I was born in Krizancevo Selo on 13th of September, 1952.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to speak slowly, please. Can I have the assistance of the usher, please, and can we have the aerial photo of Ahmici? Mrs. Milicevic, on this aerial photograph could you please point with the pointer that you have in your hand to your house, the approximate location of your house? Yes, you may remove your earphones and approach the easel.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my house here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down now. Would you please tell us whose houses are in the vicinity of your house and which Croats' houses are there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the immediate vicinity of my house there is the house of Ivo Papic, Pero Milicevic, Slavko Milicevic, Rafael.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And which Muslim houses are in the vicinity of your house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: The house of Muharem Caucevic, for example, Sutko Caucevic, Atif Ahmic's house, Latif Ahmic's house, Hamo Hodzic's house and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said you were born in the village of Krizancevo Selo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Does that village have another name as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's also called Donja Drubravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So it's the same village, Krizancevo Selo or Donja Dubravica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you came to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I came to Ahmici 17 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And up to what time did you live in Krizancevo Selo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I lived there until 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And after that? Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I went to Zenica and I spent six years in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you came to Ahmici after living in Zenica for a while?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the relations between Croats and Muslims in Ahmici before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Their relations were very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What does that mean? Would people visit each other?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: That means we got along very well all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge about the first conflict that occurred on the 20th of October, 1992, and if so, could you please tell us what you had heard about the events of that day when the incident broke out, whether you heard any shooting and so on.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: At first it seemed to be like any other day, everything was normal. However, in the early morning, that is the night between the 19th and the 20th of October, maybe around 5.00 a.m., I heard very loud shooting. I was at home, together with my husband, my two children and my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know what it was all about? Did you subsequently learn what the cause of the shooting was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I was the last one to leave the area and I was hoping that the things would calm down, but I decided to leave the house, together with my children, my husband and my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what time it was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: It was at about 5.20, 5:30. The shooting was not very intense at first but it got very intense in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that. When did you leave your house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I left my house around 9.30. I was among the last ones to leave the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you know what the reasons were for that shooting? Did you happen to learn that later on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: When I got to the shelter I learnt that the night before a roadblock had been set up across the road from the Catholic cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: On the road?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: After this shooting incident, you said that it occurred around half past five in the morning, apart from it, apart from the shooting, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. My bedroom faces the village of Ahmici, and from the direction of the mosque I heard someone say, "Croats, surrender."

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you think that it was coming from the direction of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was very foggy. I didn't see the person, I only heard a voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So it was a foggy day, it was a foggy morning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was early in the morning, dawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Normally can you see the mosque from your house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the yard and from the balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Would you hear the hodza calling for prayer from the mosque?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how long the fog stayed in the valley?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Until 9.00, half past nine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said you left the house around half past nine, together with your husband, your mother and your two children.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: We went in the direction of the nearby wood, which is some 30 metres away from our house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: We had been warned before when there was Serbian air attacks that we could seek shelter in the wood, but I went in the direction of the shelter. I went to the shelter actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where was that shelter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: It was maybe 300 metres from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What is it exactly, is it a house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a house. It has a basement and it's a house that belongs to Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you point to that house on the map, the house of Anto Bralo, where you took shelter with your family?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Here. (Indicating)

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You stated that you had taken shelter there before, during the Serbian air attacks?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Would Muslims also take shelter in that house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: During the conflict that occurred on the 20th of October, 1992, are you aware of any Muslims who left the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did all of them leave the village of Ahmici or did some stay behind?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, most of them left but they didn't stay away very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When did they come back?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: The people from the area of Gornja Ahmici came back first, but I think that within three days all of them came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did Croats invite them? Did they call them back?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the Croat leadership from the municipality urge them to come back?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My uncle Santic was the mayor of Vitez and he insisted that Muslims come back to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of any complaints made by Muslims to the effect that their houses, their property had been plundered?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You don't know or you don't think that such incidents took place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't think that such incidents took place. I'm not aware of any complaints that people made to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What were the relations between Croats and Muslims after the first conflict?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we would say hello to each other but we no longer visit each other that often, but friends were not being neglected, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You personally continued seeing your Muslim friends who were your best friends?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was on very good terms with all of them, but my first neighbours there, my closest acquaintances Ahmic, Causevic family, those who lived in my vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you continued seeing each other?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were still my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether during the first conflict anyone was killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember Halid Pezer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was there any Croat that was killed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a person by the surname of Vidovic but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: We will now move to the second conflict, and I have several questions about that conflict. On the eve of the second conflict was there anything that was indicative of what was going to happen on the following day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't notice anything. Other people didn't either. I spent the night at home and didn't notice anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What about your husband? Was he at home?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, he was working the night-shift so I was alone with my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he was working the night-shift on the night of the 15th and the 16th of April. Well, where did he work at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He was working in the Princip factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What happened on the morning of the 16th of April, 1993? What did you hear, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Around 5:20 shooting started, and on that occasion I didn't hesitate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the direction of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, not exactly, because my impression is that it was coming from all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that your husband was not there on that morning when the shooting started, that he was not at home, that he was working. So what did you decide to do?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I got up immediately, I took my children and I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I went in the usual direction, first in the direction of the wood and then to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Before that, before you reached the shelter, and you're referring to the shelter in the house of Anto Bralo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you encounter anyone on that morning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw Dragica Papic and Ivana Ruzica Papic as well, Dragan, Marija Papic, Ivo Papic, Goran Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I saw them in the wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who Dragica Papic is?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Dragica Papic is Dragan's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What about Ivana?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: She is his younger sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you saw them in the wood?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So did you go to the shelter together?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you reached the house of Anto Bralo, you intended to go to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What did they say? Where were they going?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Dragan and Ruzica, they continued in the direction of Rovna. And his mother and his sister went there. Well, they continued on the road; I didn't know where they would stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: They didn't tell you anything where they were going?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice or did you know that Dragan's wife, Ruzica, was pregnant?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she was pregnant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: On that day, did you see any other women and children leave their homes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, and I learned later on that they had left with their children. So I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to the whereabouts of Dragan Papic on that day, on the 16th of April, and do you know where he was during the following days? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: We were afraid that the water was polluted, so I went to the well every day, and I would see Dragan every day near the Radakovo Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where did you go to get water?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I went to the village of Rovna. There is a natural source of water there, and I would go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So it is not from the River Lasva, but from a natural spring of water that was in the area?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said you saw Dragan near the Radakovo Bridge; what was he doing there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were afraid that the bridge would be blown up, and that was our only means of escape, that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So there was a lot of shooting in the area?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there was a lot of shooting, and the area was not safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else with Dragan on that particular occasion when you went to fetch the water?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Ivo Vidovic was there, and another person whom I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said you'd gone to Gornja Rovna and that you'd crossed the Radakovo Bridge in order to get to the spring?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any other people on the other side, people who were watching over the bridge?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Zvonko Santic there, and Jozo Alilovic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else with them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: There were other individuals who were there, but I knew these two people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you didn't know anyone else?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, or later on, did you get back to your house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I would go to my house during the night, and I would stay in the shelter during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you only went to your house to check -- to check the situation, and then you would go back to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: That evening, when you came to see your house to see what had happened, did anyone come to you? Did you have any contacts with anyone on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, I went to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you about that very same day, the 16th of April: Did you go back to your house on that day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And did you see anyone there on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Goran Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why did he come to your house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to spend the night there, and he told me that the situation was not safe. My husband was still at work. He couldn't come home, so I was not really protected in any way. And he told me that it would be better for me to go back to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So your husband could not come home; he spent 15 days at work?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So after the conflict had broken out, he had to stay there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: During the following days, did any soldiers come to your house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the day of the 16th of April, and do you recall how Dragan Papic was dressed on that day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: It was very dark, and the visibility was not very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When you met him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All I could notice was that he had an upper part of a camouflage uniform and he had civilian trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But when you went to fetch the water, was he wearing the same type of clothes, the same as you had noticed the previous morning? When he was standing guard, was he wearing the same type of camouflage shirt and civilian trousers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any insignia on the camouflage shirt?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When you went to the spring to get the water, did he have any weapons while he was at the Radakovo Bridge?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he had a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What about the other guard? You said Ivo Vidovic was there as well; did he have a rifle too?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what type of car Dragan had during that period of time, 1992, 1993?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I -- I don't easily distinguish between cars. I had a Stojadin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Stojadin is a Zastava 101 type of vehicle?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And Dragan was repairing cars, so I know that he had a Stojadin as well, because occasionally, when we needed, he would give us some spare parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the colour of the car, his car?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a yellow car. Ours was white and his was yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You were his neighbour; did you see him drive any other cars?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, since he was repairing vehicles, he would test them, and he would drive various vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he would try the vehicles after repairing them, to check if everything was right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time see any kind of weapon in front of the house of Dragan Papic, anti-aircraft gun, anti-aircraft machine gun, or did you hear anything about such weapons being there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, there is only one small road between our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How far is your house from his house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: About 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about any shooting, any fire being opened from their house, from a sniper rifle or any other type of weapon? Would you have heard if such thing had happened?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, normally I would have heard, but we had left our houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but even -- was there any shooting, was there any fire that was opened?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I don't think so. I don't think that anyone would let him do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You told us who lived with you in your house; you mentioned a couple of your neighbours. And I would like to know whether you know Abdulah Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know Muris Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How about Mehmed Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I know him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us if they were related in any way? Abdulah Ahmic and Muris Ahmic, for example?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: They were cousins. Their parents were brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So Abdulah Ahmic and Muris Ahmic are brothers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And Abdulah Ahmic and Muris Ahmic are cousins to Mehmed Ahmic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I now want to ask you something about Abdulah Ahmic. Could you tell us what kind of person Abdulah Ahmic was? What was your impression of him? You used to see him often?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did. He is a very quiet person. He is not very sociable; he's quite reserved. But I don't think that he would harm anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see him with other people, in company of some other people?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So not even in company of other Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: During this armed conflict, did you lose any of your close relatives?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who did you lose?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I lost my brother and my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What was the name of your brother?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: His name was Rudolf Krizanac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where was he killed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He was killed at Bohine Kuce.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when he was killed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He was killed on the 8th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about other people being killed there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, several people were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that your brother-in-law was killed as well; what was his name?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Milicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where was he killed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He was killed at Kuber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When? If you know that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: It was in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said you were born in Krizancevo Selo or in the village of Dubravica; do you know what happened in Krizancevo Selo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. On the 22nd of December, 1993, Muslim forces attacked the village, and they killed two shifts of people. I think that 74 Croats were killed. 22 of them were from my family, from the Krizanac family, and I know that 74 people were buried on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said it was in late 1993?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: That is on the 22nd of December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who lives in the village of Krizancevo Selo now?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: There are not many men left; most of them are elderly people. One of my brothers was killed, but I still have four brothers who live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was the village destroyed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but -- and I think that people did not come back for about one year. But most of the houses were rebuilt in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How far is Krizancevo Selo from Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: About three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I have a few questions regarding Dragan Papic. What could you tell us about Dragan Papic? Did you know him well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him very well. We used to see each other every day. And I can say that he's a very sociable person, he's an easy-going person. He likes to make jokes. He's not prone to any conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see or hear him quarrel with anyone, or --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, on the contrary. He always tried to make people laugh.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was he on good terms with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He made no distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who he was on particularly good terms with among the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he spent a lot of time with Samir Causevic. For years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were they of the same age?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were the same generation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: He's a Muslim, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was he close with other Muslims later on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: More recently he met Nusret Paco, and he spent quite a bit of time with him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: And who was Nusret Paco? Where did he come from?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Nusret is a refugee from Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Has he settled somewhere in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he settled in Hamo Hodzic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was this a weekend home?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I gave them the keys.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you held the keys of this man's weekend home? And where did Hamo Hodzic live?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Across the road to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: I mean permanently?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He lived in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you mediate, in a sense, in that friendship?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I introduced them. They were of the same age, they exchanged visits, they had an understanding. They assisted one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice anything in particular about Dragan doing something helpful for Nusret Paco?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It touched me, because he was very attentive of the baby. So Dragan and his wife brought milk, because Paco had a two-month-old baby; and to avoid the baby being given powdered milk, Dragan and his wife would bring the baby natural milk.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What happened to Nusret Paco?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: He was killed, was he?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who buried him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Ivo Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: That's Dragan's father, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How were you personally affected by this death of Nusret Paco?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: We were deeply distressed, yes. His mother came that morning and asked us to bury him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Dragan Papic's wedding with Ruzica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there many Muslims present?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: There may have even been more Muslims than Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were they all on good terms? Did they have a good time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we all did, all of us together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did anyone take photographs of that wedding, of the party?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Mehmed Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How did he record the event?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I think he had a video camera, and I think there's a videotape of that wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was it his camera?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was his own property.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dragan Papic ever, speaking to you or anyone else, said anything against the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I never heard him do so. I think he didn't really have any understanding of politics. It did not concern him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Afterwards would he mention in your company Nusret and his death? Did he comment on it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I know that he was horrified. He was very sad. I visited his tomb myself. I missed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So you do not recollect Dragan saying anything that could be nationalistic, that could be directed against the Muslims or any comments on political issues?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What was his hobby? What was his main interest?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Whose do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Dragan.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: You mean Dragan. Cars were his main hobby.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he repaired cars.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Whoever came to ask for his assistance. He was happiest when working on a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Dragan Papic was employed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: In Sumarija, the forestry company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So this was a company based in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long he remained employed in Sumarija?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of the war did Dragan Papic wear a beard?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you see Dragan Papic here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you see a beard on him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was the beard he used to wear bigger than he's wearing now?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, significantly bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he come to see you in connection with his beard?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I cut it for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there any remarks by people regarding his beard?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His parents didn't like it, but he considered it part of his image.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you try to persuade him to shave it off?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had had enough of cutting it for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when his wife Ruzica had delivered?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: How come you're so sure of that date the 28th of April? What year was that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: That was '83.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You mean '93?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What makes you so sure?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I go regularly to the birthday parties of Dragan's child.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What's the child's name, the one that was born on the 28th of April?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: The name is Marin Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where was he born?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: In Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why was he born there? Why did Ruzica, Dragan's wife, go to deliver her baby in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Because the midwife was a highly skilled one and she trusted her. Ruzica trusted her.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Ulfeta Luco.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is she a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, she is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about Dragan's father Ivo Papic? What kind of a man was he and how did he treat the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. For me and everyone else he is, to this day, close to Muslims. He's a plumber by occupation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the building of the mosque in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did the Croats of Ahmici give any kind of assistance in the construction of that mosque?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I know Asim Ahmic, the owner, the mosque was built on state-owned land, he asked permission from the Croats, and I know that Hasim Ahmic also donated some land for our cemetery, so that he was given permission by the Croats and the mosque was built unhindered, with the approval of Croats and Muslims, on state-owned land.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was there a big celebration when the mosque was opened?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there many guests from other places too?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there many cars and buses?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know that the Croats allowed parking space to be used for cars and buses that came.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Ivo Papic, Dragan's father, actually worked on the construction of that mosque?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He fitted the plumbing for the mosque. There's another mosque about 150 metres away and he did the plumbing for that one too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So he did so free of charge?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was his contribution to the construction of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Are the Muslims returning to Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Has quite a number of them come back?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, as many as 99 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Are they still asking Ivo Papic to do plumbing work in their homes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know. Wherever Muslims returned, the -- Ivo repaired the water supply, and in the Mehurici settlement which is also inhabited by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: So this is during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Even now. Tolovici, Grbavica, Mehurici Busovaca Ahmici. He does work on the water supply system that is providing water for both Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see a flag on Ivo Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: What kind of flag?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: The Croatian flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: On which occasions was this flag hoisted?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: On festivities like Christmas, Easter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: On any other religious occasions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did other Croats also fly flags?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did Muslims fly their own flags on their celebrations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, the crescent and star flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: You said that before the conflict with the Muslims you would see Dragan in uniform, I think you said.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see what kind of uniform he had? Was it complete uniform?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He would change. Most frequently he would wear a forester's uniform, then a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you see him wearing a black uniform sometimes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Was it just the top part?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Mostly the top part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Were there any insignia on that black uniform?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Nothing that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Why did he wear that? Did he perhaps ever mention the reason to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No. I never really found out. I didn't notice any insignia. I never gave the matter any thought actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did he perhaps mention that it was easier for him to move around wearing those clothes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He wore a camouflage uniform believing he gained an importance thereby and he would have lesser problems when moving around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know how he obtained that black uniform?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I know I was having coffee at Dragan Papic's house, it was summertime, and there is a table outside and we were drinking coffee, and a relative of mine came by. Dragan was repairing his car, and on the bench there was a bag with something inside, and Dragan put it on immediately and started working. But the dark colour suited him, so I didn't make any distinction whether it was a camouflage uniform or a black uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: But this dark uniform suited him because he would get dirty repairing cars?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And he would move around in those clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you know of other young men putting on similar camouflage uniforms or other kinds of clothing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because they felt more comfortable. Even elderly people who didn't belong to any military units would wear such clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any Muslims also wearing camouflage uniforms without belonging to military units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone in particular from Ahmici, a Muslim, wearing a camouflage uniform? Can you recollect anyone?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Fahrudin Ahmic, Fahran we call him. Yes, Fahrudin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Where did Fahrudin Ahmic live?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Across the way to Marija Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Is he alive?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PULISELIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have completed my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Puliselic. You may have noticed that I have not objected to quite a few leading questions you've put, and I have realised that also the Prosecutor had no objection. I wonder now whether the -- Counsel Pavkovic can tell us whether any other Defence counsel is prepared to cross-examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the other Defence counsel do not have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. So I will call upon then the Prosecutor. Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mrs. Milicevic, I appear for the Prosecution. I appear with Mr. Frank Terrier and Mr. Michael Blaxill, and I will it's my role in these proceedings to ask you a few questions about the testimony you've given today.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we ask counsel to speak into the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And it's my role to ask you some questions about the evidence you've given today. Do you understand that? Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Mrs. Milicevic, when did you first discover that Dragan Papic was indicted in relation to these charges?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Prior to coming to court today, have you spoken to any other person, apart from the lawyers for Dragan Papic in this case, about what you would be saying in court today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So you haven't spoken to Ivica Vidovic about your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Or Zvonimir Santic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I haven't met him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned a Zvonko Santic and that I think you saw at the Radak Bridge. Who is Zvonko Santic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: My neighbour --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: -- across the other side of the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And is his full name Zvonimir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I think it is. I call him Zvonko, but I'm not sure of his full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And have you spoken to Zvonko about the proceedings prior to today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No. I haven't seen him since the war, truly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And Goran Papic, have you spoken to him about your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I haven't seen him even, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You mentioned that on the 16th of April you heard some, I think, gunfire at about 5.30, and then as a result of that --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I said about 5.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And as a result of that you immediately left your house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. In the second conflict, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And your husband was at work, but I think your two children were still at home?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with me during the second conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And how old are your two children?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Sixteen. That was my son, he was sixteen, and the little girl was eight at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And your son, was he in the village guard at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, he was underage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did your son have a rifle or a weapon of some sort?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And your husband, was he in the village guard?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, when he came back 15 days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You are aware that Muslims and Croats from the village of Ahmici and Santici patrolled the village prior to the 16th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And this -- when did this village guard first start?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: When the Serb air force started.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that would have been about April 1992?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In the beginning, the village guard, was it a mixed guard with Muslims and Croats or were there two groups?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Were they two separate groups that worked together, or, in fact, was it one group made up of a combination of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: At first they were together. Afterwards they separated. At first they were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So at first there was a --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: -- one organisation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Together. Yes, yes. Joint organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And in the beginning who was the coordinator of the village guard?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I just know that they organised themselves. They were self-organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And what area did the village guard cover in the beginning when it was a joint organisation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Simply Ahmici, our houses; I don't know how to put it. A small area, maybe 100 metres in diameter. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The Croat residence from middle Ahmici, for example, Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic, were they a part of that village guard in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And that was the same village guard that your husband belonged to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, my husband was there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you're aware of Mr. Nenad Santic, who used to live in the village?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You know Mr. Nenad Santic? You knew him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And he was in that same village guard that your husband was in, and the Kupreskics; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So the village guard extended more than just 100 metres from your house; it included the area of Ahmici and Santici and some parts of Pirici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Nadioci was separate. I don't understand. Pirici? Pirici above the Kupreskic's houses were Muslims. But I'm repeating, for a time we were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when did that village guard split between -- on ethnic lines, between Croats and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I would not be able to tell you the exact date. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: But after the conflict on the 20th of October, in 1992, the village guard definitely split after that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I must repeat, I don't know; I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think you said --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I do not have any knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I think you said in your evidence that after the conflict on the 20th of October, relations in the village between Muslims and Croats cooled somewhat.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And the fighting in that village would have had quite a drastic effect on the people that lived in the village?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Prior to the 16th of April, in any event, the Croat village guard operated outside of the Muslim village guard? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The Croats guarded the village separately just before the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And your husband was a member of that village guard?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was. But on the evening of the 16th, he went to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And your husband had a weapon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You said on the morning --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Because he was at work for 15 days, so he didn't have one. No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: But you had one -- I'm asking whether he had one at his house, at your house. Did he have --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: In the second conflict? Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: You stated that you got up on the morning of the 16th after you heard the shooting; I assume you got up and left your house because you were scared. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you had no knowledge of any impending conflict on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you immediately went to Anto Bralo's house, which I think is near Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And did you go to Anto Bralo's house with your son as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No, he stayed in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And when he stayed in the woods, did he have a weapon with him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: No. No, he's a child; they wouldn't let him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And why did he stay in the woods and not go to Anto Bralo's house with you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Simply he was an adolescent at the time, and he didn't want to go with me, his mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What did he say to you? What did he want to in fact do?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean? I don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I assume that you went to Anto Bralo's house for some personal safety.

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, and my little girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And I assume that you would have been concerned that your son would have had that same personal safety that you wanted for yourself and your daughter?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did you ask him to come with you, and did he refuse?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: So he wasn't particularly scared about what was going on around in the village at that time? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: He was scared. He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: What was his purpose of staying in the forest?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Because Goran Papic was there, his friend, the same age. Ivo Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Could you mention again how many people you saw in the forest when you first got there, before going to Anto Bralo's house?

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: There aren't many of us there anyway. There was Ivo and Goran, and that's all, as far as I could see. But in the shelter, I saw Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: And you said earlier that you saw Dragica Papic, Dragan's mother; Ivana, Dragan's sister; and Ruzica --

utterances.speaker: LJUBICA MILICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, they were, but they left. They went to Rovna. But I stayed in the shelter of Anto Bralo, and Ivo, Goran, stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Did Dragan leave first from the group in the forest, or did you leave before they did?
